summary: This round resolves most of round 1. The temp tests now cover the security branches on the control plane, the error messages and sign-in button on the setup page, the routing outside the sign-in gate, the WebHost wiring, and the ordering of handoff redemption before the setup read. The stray log files are gone, and I accept the coverage exemptions for moved code and type declarations. The coverage gate still fails on 4 changed lines that are neither covered nor exempt: IntegrationSetupPage.tsx:51 and 101, and mountHaloApp.tsx:7 and 30.

findings.body: setupHandoff.test.ts now tests setupReader's ordering well. The page's own wiring is still unexercised: the query function that calls `readSetup()` (line 51) never runs. That wiring includes the reader built from the `#handoff=` fragment at lines 39-45. Every page test seeds the query cache, so nothing checks that the page redeems the handoff from the URL before reading. Add a temp test that runs the query function: render with a `#handoff=...` hash and a fresh QueryClient, or call `client.fetchQuery` after mounting. Assert that redeemHandoff runs before read. Line 101 (`await setup.refetch()`) is an unchanged line that was only re-indented. A coverage-exempt marker with that reason is acceptable there.

HaloAppRoutes.test.tsx now tests the route tree, which resolves the original concern. Lines 7 (the import) and 30 (`<HaloAppRoutes host={host} />`) are still uncovered and have no exemption, so the gate fails. A coverage-exempt marker is acceptable here, with a reason such as: thin composition shell; HaloAppRoutes is tested directly. Otherwise, add a temp test that mounts the app.

testRequests.target: packages/web/src/IntegrationSetupPage.tsx:39-51 — the page reads the handoff from window.location.hash and its query function redeems it before api.read
testRequests.rationale: This is the only page-level wiring of the handoff-before-read ordering, and no test runs it.
